free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

egress.terms: This IS the egress allowance: 1 TB/month free to the internet from 300+ PoPs, worldwide except China PoPs.

tooling: CloudFront distributions in front of any HTTP origin (S3, an OCI VM, a block-volume nginx); terraform/CLI; signed URLs and signed cookies for access control.
chaining: CloudFront can use any publicly accessible URL as its origin, so it can front a non-AWS origin, such as another provider's free tier, and serve cacheable responses from edge locations.

limits.value: 1 TB data transfer out and 10 Million HTTP or HTTPS requests per month, always free; usage beyond it is billed

limits_note: Separately from the always-free allowance, CloudFront flat-rate plans carry a monthly data transfer allowance of 100GB (Free), 50TB (Pro), 50TB (Business) and 50TB (Premium, configurable up to 600TB for a new flat-rate price). Beyond the always-free allowance, pay-as-you-go usage is billed.

extras.verified_at_basis: vendor pages read on 2026-11-03: https://aws.amazon.com/free/networking/ and https://aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/pricing/; the sign-up requirements were not read
extras.quota_verbatim: 1 TB/month data transfer out + 10,000,000 HTTP/HTTPS requests + 2,000,000 CloudFront Function invocations, free every month, explicitly 'no longer limited to the first 12 months after signup'.
extras.limits_verbatim: 1 TB/month is 1/15th of a 500 GB/day workload (≈15 TB/month). Beyond that it is metered at standard CloudFront rates. Origin fetch traffic still hits the origin's own egress meter (so pairing it with Oracle means Oracle's 10 TB absorbs the cache misses).
extras.egress_verbatim: This IS the egress allowance: 1 TB/month free to the internet from 300+ PoPs, worldwide except China PoPs.
extras.chaining_verbatim: 1 TB/month free egress per AWS account. Because it is a pull-through cache in front of an arbitrary origin, it can front a NON-AWS origin — so in principle it can serve the 150 GB Oracle block volume or any other free tier, absorbing 1 TB/month of the ~500 GB/day serving load. It stacks with Oracle's own 10 TB/month.
extras.tooling_verbatim: CloudFront distributions in front of any HTTP origin (S3, an OCI VM, a block-volume nginx); terraform/CLI; signed URLs and signed cookies for access control.
extras.agent_focus: Big-cloud free tiers and always-free/credit programmes, judged on >=500GB free per unit, free egress, and programmatic access

binding_note: data transfer out is free only up to 1 TB per month; the allowance is a monthly volume, not a daily one
